catalog_quote: 2.5 Tone. Sougb has most likely a pitch-accent system. There are a number of monosyllabic lexical items which contrast in tone. But even in the case of multiple homophones, I could only detect two tone levels ... The consistent realisation of (15) and (16) by three speakers suggests that ou 'to wear' has low tone, and ou 'to greet' has lexically high. ... The following examples suggest that the pitch on the free pronoun and the final syllable of eidja is irrelevant, with the contrastive pitch located on the first syllable of the verb. ... It is obvious that much more detailed research would be needed to make a definitive statement on the relevance of tone in Sougb. At this moment, all that can be said is that Sougb has at least two contrastive tones, which operate as a pitch-accent system. audit.reasoning: Quote confirmed verbatim in the PL-524 copy we hold at the stated pages (sketch sec. 2.5, pp.194-196; volume sec. 7.1, p.26). The deciding source is the fullest description of the language (96-pp Pacific Linguistics sketch by the fieldworker, 2002) and nothing newer on Sougb phonology/prosody exists in Glottolog 5.1, Crossref or Semantic Scholar; the later UNIPA theses are all morphosyntax. The downloaded NUSA 47 (2000) precursor by the same author agrees (pitch accent, two tone levels, tone on one syllable per polysyllabic word, which he there calls 'the stressed syllable') and, like the sketch, states no stress-placement rule, so tonal-OR-pitch accent with empty the rule as stated stands. Reesink's own hedge (analysis provisional; possibly more than two levels) is already carried in tone_note. Minor bookkeeping only: the record's 'held' field is empty although the PDF is held by the project at our earlier reading

sources.quote: 'Sougb has a pitch-accent system with two levels of tone, yielding a number of minimal pairs, such as mog 'thorn, sharp' and mog 'flesh'. On polysyllabic words, only the stressed syllable is specified for a certain tone.' Also p.107: -ec 'with high tone: sneeze, peel, open, light, shoot; with a low tone: walk, pick'. No statement of where stress falls.
sources.locator: p.105 (language introduction preceding the text), PDF page 105
sources.note: Only other first-hand description of Sougb prosody; its one-paragraph phonology note says tone is specified only on 'the stressed syllable' of polysyllabic words, which sharpens the record's domain note (tone-bearing = stressed syllable) without giving a stress-placement rule.
